newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to issue new licences for Islamic banks.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to issue new licences for Islamic banks.

text.p: Malaysia plans to issue new banking licences to create one or two new Islamic banks, a central Bank Negara official said on Wednesday.
"We are considering to have one, two more Islamic banks," said Bank Negara Assistant Governor Abdul Murad Khalid. "These are separate new ones, new licences."
He said the new institutions will provide competition to Malaysia's sole Islamic bank, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd.
"They will create more players, more competition," Abdul Murad said.
He said there was also a big potential for other Islamic financial institutions in Malaysia.

Bank Islam, set up in 1984, has pioneered Malaysia's Moslem banking system which is based on the principle of profit-sharing among banks and clients. Paying and accepting interest is considered usury under Islam.
Malaysia has frozen commercial banking licences in order to prod the country's 37 banks to merge and become more competitive as the country's financial markets are liberalised
Analysts say Malaysia, with a population of about 21 million, is "overbanked", that there are too many banks supporting too few customers.

But Abdul Murad, speaking on the sidelines of an Islamic capital market conference, said the proportion of Islamic banking deposits in Malaysia was still small, at around two percent of total deposits.
The government wants the Islamic system deposits to rise to "five percent by the year 2000", he said.
In its 1996 annual report, Bank Negara said Islamic banking deposits totalled 7.26 billion ringgit at end-1996, up 47.5 percent from the previous year.
